newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan eyes Ishigaki, Japan for China transshipment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan eyes Ishigaki, Japan for China transshipment.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party has proposed turning Japan's southern island of Ishigaki into a transshipment centre for restricted trade with rival China after Hong Kong comes under Beijing's rule in July.
"Use Ishigaki as a transshipment centre for the mainland," the United Daily News on Tuesday quoted party business management committee chief Liu Tai-ying as saying.

Taiwan has banned direct transport, communications and other official links with communist China for nearly five decades but faces mounting pressure from Taiwan firms that operate on the mainland to ease the restriction.
Some 25,000 Taiwan firms have poured some US$20 billion into China since an unofficial thaw a decade ago made this possible and indirect trade across the Taiwan strait has soared.
Hong Kong remains the main transshipment centre for cargoes moving between Taiwan and China, but Taiwan is actively hunting a possible alternative as the British colony's handover looms.
Taiwan fears that Beijing -- which takes control of Hong Kong in July -- could exploit Taiwan's heavy reliance on the territory to squeeze it for political concessions.
Beijing regards Taiwan as a renegade province and has been turning up pressure on Taipei to accept Beijing's sovereignty and reunify.
Ishigaki lies west of Japan's southernmost major island of Okinawa, just (240 km) 150 miles east of Taiwan's northern Chilung port and only 35 minutes away by air.
Ishigaki is closer than Hong Kong to China's major eastern and northern ports at Shanghai, Fuzhou, Tianjin and Dalian.
Taiwan's government regularly warns of overdependence on China's booming economy and has urged diversification of investment to southeast Asia and elsewhere in the region.

The Nationalist Party, one of the world's richest with some T$37.8 billion (US$1.4 billion) in assets under the committee's management, has launched a new drive to steer Taiwan investment toward nearby areas other than rival China.
This includes a high-profile drive to invest in Okinawa, Japan's least-developed region and one where Liu and his panel will lead a business development mission later in December.
